main_text.p: das Thamarem nurum suam jußit vi-duam domi paterna manere, donec Iudæ filius Sela adoleviffet, veritus ne & is mo-reretur ficut ejus fratres. Igitur Thamar domum paternam se recepit, ibiq; fuit. Genes 38.

Tum Moses inde digreffus, ad Iethro-nem socerum suum reversus est, & ab eo petivit, ut sibi ad consanguineos suos, qui essent in Aegypto, redire liceret, & providere, utrum adhuc viverent: quem Iethro cum bona pace dimisit. Moses igitur à Iova in Madiania admonitus, ut Aegyptum repeteret (mortuos enim esse omnes illos qui ejus vitam petebant) uxorē suam adhibet, & filios, eisq; in asinum illatis, in Aegyptum redire contendit, divinam illam virgam secum ferens. E-xodi 4.

p.i: Ad consanguineum suum ne quis vestrum accedito, ut ejus naturam detegat. Hæc ego Iova, Patris aut matris

page.notes: Running head "NVPTIADES" is partly obscured in the scan and the printed page number "473" (shown with a fraction-like mark at the top right) is uncertain. The opening word "das" is uncertain. The heading "LXIII" and "LXIIII" are set in spaced capitals and are copied as bare numbers. The chapter numbers are shown with a small mark above the letters, which is not transcribed. The text breaks mid-sentence at the foot of the page; the continuation is on the following page.
